full_judgment: 20. Mr Razik Al Jalil, the learned advocate appearing for respondent Nos. 1-3, and Dr. Shahdeen Malik, the learned advocate appearing for respondent No.5, both of them opted to adopt the submissions advanced by Mr. Murad Reza. However, Dr. Malik, added a further submission that respondent Nos. 1-4 are government functionaries and in course of carrying out their routine tasks they have made a decision in favour of respondent No.5 in accordance with law and it is the settled principle of law that presumption on the decision made by a government functionary should be that the same has been taken bonafide unless any aggrieved person makes out a clear case of malafide by categorically stating the motive or dishonesty of the concerned government functionary. He submits that there is no specific allegation against the respondents in leveling blame against them that they have been influenced by extraneous consideration. By referring to the case of Farzana Haque vs University of Dhaka 42 DLR 262, he submits that malafide must be pleaded in clearer terms in a writ petition and requires to be proved by material evidence and, thus, malafide must not be readily inferred. By making the aforesaid submissions, the learned advocate for the respondents pray for discharging the Rule.
